title:
A Markdown collapsible is a section with a title and body, where the body can be expanded/collapsed. This uses
the `details` HTML element for rendering.

```md
+++ Spoiler
The _butler_ did it.
+++
```

+++ Spoiler
The _butler_ did it.
+++

To make the collapsible initially expanded, the last plus sign should be a `>` (and this is included in the length
for nesting purposes):

```md
++> Spoiler
The _butler_ did it.
+++
```

++> Spoiler
The _butler_ did it.
+++

Collapsibles are implemented using the HTML `details` element.

# Accordions

Also, a series of these in a row _without_ terminating lines between creates an "accordion", where only one of the
sections may be open at a time:

```md
+++ First Act
Characters introduced, initial plot unfolds.
+++ Second Act
Plot complication, minor drama.
+++ Third Act
Additional complication, major drama, resolution.
+++
```

+++ First Act
Characters introduced, initial plot unfolds.
+++ Second Act
Plot complication, minor drama.
+++ Third Act
Additional complication, major drama, resolution.
+++

These are implemented using multiple `details` elements with the same name.

One of the sections can be initially open using `++>` as in any collapsible (see above).

# Non-exclusive Accordions

A sequence of collapsibles _with_ terminating lines between creates a non-exclusive accordion, where multiple
sections may be open. (This is essentially just a series of collapsibles.)

```md
+++ First Act
Characters introduced, initial plot unfolds.
+++
+++ Second Act
Plot complication, minor drama.
+++
+++ Third Act
Additional complication, major drama, resolution.
+++
```

+++ First Act
Characters introduced, initial plot unfolds.
+++
+++ Second Act
Plot complication, minor drama.
+++
+++ Third Act
Additional complication, major drama, resolution.
+++

Any of the sections can be initially open using `++>` (see above).
